title: Cobalt Logistics — Edge Terraform roadmap (draft)
content:
Context: Cobalt Logistics is evaluating a hybrid private deployment (VPC + on-prem edge nodes) to run Redwood Inference for low-latency routing in distribution centers. This document captures a working roadmap for the Terraform modules, sizing assumptions, upgrade path and Q&A we will use for the customer-facing SOW and the internal runbook.

High-level goals (customer asks):
- <= 20ms median token latency for local inference in regional DCs for short-chat workload (typical prompt 128 tokens).
- Predictable per-node throughput: target 400 concurrent short requests per GPU at 75% p95 latency SLO.
- Strict data residency: inference traffic must terminate inside customer VPC; logs to be forwarded to customer SIEM.
- Zero-downtime minor upgrades and automated rollback for major upgrades.

Primary constraints identified:
- On-prem racks have 2x A100 80GB per chassis (older BIOS), BMC access is throttled during business hours.
- Customer network: regional VPCs connected by AWS Direct Connect + private MPLS fallback. MTU 1500, limited jumbo frames.
- Air-gapped edge site (Site C) will not have access to public container registries; we must provide offline image bundles.

Assumptions used for sizing (call out for review):
- Baseline model: small Llama2-Chat variant running with 4-bit quantization. Avg generation per request 64 tokens.
- Effective throughput per A100 @ q4_0: 450 concurrent short-chat requests (measured internal bench, 90% pkts). We apply 0.7 safety factor for production -> 315 concurrent.
- We target 1.5x headroom on peak to allow bursts.
- Persistence: 2-node control-plane per region (HA) + 3x serving nodes per region minimum.
- Storage: model artifacts stored on NFS backed by customer storage, initial delta ~ 1.2TB per model (quantized).

Proposed node footprint (per region):
- Control plane: 2x m5.large (or equivalent VMs) in customer VPC for state services (k8s control-plane-lite).
- Serving nodes: 3x chassis (each chassis = 2x A100 80GB) -> treat as 6 logical GPUs. With safety factor gives ~1890 concurrent capacity at model target.
- If multiple model variants (fallback smaller model), include capacity to run both simultaneously: +1 chassis for canary/fallback.

Terraform module notes (module names and responsibilities):
- module.vpc-flat: create and validate customer VPC peering, route tables, security groups (egress-only to ops endpoints), and Direct Connect configs. NOTE: this module intentionally creates no public IPs.
- module.k8s-edge-lite: spins up hardened k8s nodes for control plane and nodepools; integrates with customer CNI (Calico) and uses hostNetworking for serving pods where required.
- module.gpu-serverset: defines GPU node groups, device plugin config, and node labels for autoscaler; exposes inputs for per-node GPU counts and chassis metadata.
- module.model-artifacts: manages model artifact lifecycle for offline sync (tar + checksum), pre-warm hooks, and retention policy. Must support two transfer modes: rsync-over-sftp and signed OCI bundle.
- module/ops-integrations: log forwarding (syslog/otlp), KMS/HSM key references (customer-managed keys), and VPN/Direct Connect endpoints.

Key implementation decisions / open questions:
- Offline images: deliver as OCI bundles vs tarballs + local registry. Preferred: OCI bundles signed and shipped on encrypted USB for air-gapped site, but customer asked for scripts to import into their Harbor registry. Action: create module.model-artifacts.importer script and document step-by-step.
- KMS integration: customer uses AWS KMS for VPC sites and Thales HSM for on-prem. We will surface a generic KMS ref in module.ops-integrations and provide two example providers. Need security review for HSM drivers.
- Node bootstrapping: customer restricts external SSH during business hours; we need an init window (02:00-05:00 local) and failover plan to apply changes during allowed windows.

Upgrade plan (minor vs major):
- Minor (patch / kernel / runtime): rolling restart of serving pods with readiness probes; automatic canary on 10% of traffic for 15 minutes. If errors < 0.5% and latency within delta, proceed. Terraform: plan->apply with validate=true and an automated drift check.
- Major (runtime or model architecture changes): staged rollout: (1) dev lab > (2) customer acceptance cluster (non-prod) > (3) 1 production region as canary > (4) rest of regions. Auto-rollback via new 'release-coordinator' operator that watches health metrics (latency, error-rate, model-decoder mismatches).
- Backups: pre-upgrade snapshot of model artifacts and control-plane etcd snapshot. Data retention policy for snapshots stored encrypted off-site (customer S3).

Testing and validation matrix (what to run where):
- Smoke: infer basic prompt/response, KV-cache correctness, token continuity.
- Perf: 128-token generation p50/p95/p99 under synthetic workload. Baseline thresholds: p95 < 80ms for local model path.
- Chaos: simulate 20% node loss and observe autoscaler response within 120s.
- Security: KMS sign/verify cycle, log forwarder test to SIEM, host hardening checklist.

Rollout checklist (pre-deploy):
- Confirm rack BIOS/driver baseline and firmware (docs attached to CR).
- Obtain offline OCI bundles and complete Harbor import dry-run in staging.
- Network smoke: ensure Direct Connect L2 path and egress ACLs allow ops endpoints and customer SIEM.
- Run terraform plan with dry-run and double-sign by Eng + Customer infra lead.

Rollback playbook (if major failure):
- Step 0: stop traffic to canary region via smart-routing policy (console route override).
- Step 1: restore model artifact snapshot and redeploy previous image tag to serving nodes.
- Step 2: rollback terraform to previously committed state (documented commit hash).
- Step 3: postmortem template and follow-up actions; schedule L2/L3 postmortem with customer.

Architecture Q&A (notes from customer kickoff):
Q: "Can we run multiple model families and keep data separation?"
A: Yes — namespace-level isolation in k8s + separate model-artifact mounts and KMS keys per namespace; recommend dedicated nodepools for high-risk models.

Q: "What happens during a region-to-region network partition?"
A: Local inference continues, control-plane ops degraded. We recommend local control-plane HA and a fallback policy that pins requests to local model variants. Data sync queued for reconciling when links restore.

Q: "How will billing/usage be measured?"
A: We will enable token-level metrics export to the customer's billing pipeline (OTLP). For Dedicated/private, we export aggregated per-node token counts nightly to a signed CSV in S3.

Security / Compliance notes:
- Audit logs: operator actions (terraform apply, chart upgrades) will be forwarded to customer SIEM.
- Key rotation: cloud-side KMS keys rotated per customer policy; on-prem HSM rotation manual with playbook.
- Compliance: PSP/PodSecurity/admission controller configured; ensure export of required audit fields to meet SOC2 request (customer asked).

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Marina: produce SOW draft with proposed node counts and cost estimate (due 2026-03-05).
- Diego: prototype module.model-artifacts.importer and offline bundle instructions (WIP).
- Aisha: validate HSM integration and get security sign-off (TBD).
- Connor: run perf bench on the quantized model with current in-lab BIOS: capture p50/p95 curves (due 2026-02-20 done).

Open risks:
- Firmware issues on customer chassis may reduce achievable throughput; contingency: plan for 1 extra chassis per region as buffer.
- Air-gap delivery complexity could delay Site C by 2-3 weeks; recommend early shipping of OCI bundles.
- Customer's strict change windows will complicate upgrades — factor calendar into SOW SLAs.

Notes to self (informal):
- Need to add sample terraform input file (tfvars) for customer-specific parameters (direct_connect_id, harbor_registry_url, hsm_key_alias).
- Add a small diagram (draw.io) showing network flow for Direct Connect + MPLS fallback.
- Follow up on PR #214 for module naming conventions (avoid nested module names causing apply ordering issues).

Attachments / references:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-PLAT-4827 (private deployments patterns)
- GitHub: terraform-modules/pull/214 (device-plugin ordering fix)
- Jira: JIRA-DEPLOY-1392 (Cobalt trial onboarding)

Draft status: This is a working draft intended for internal review and for first-pass with Cobalt infra. Expect 2–3 iterations as we validate HSM and offline bundle flow.

-- Marina
